title: Scaling a sub-Gaussian variable
statement: Let $X$ be a real-valued measurable function on a measurable space with measure $bbr$, and suppose its moment-generating function satisfies the sub-Gaussian bound with variance proxy $csigma$ for every real parameter. For every $c\in\bbr$, the function $cX$ satisfies the same bound with variance proxy $c^2\sigma$.
hypotheses_covered: $X$ has sub-Gaussian moment-generating function bound with proxy $\sigma\ge 0$
replaced:
Let $X$ be a real random variable on a measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$ that is sub-Gaussian
with variance proxy $\sigma \ge 0$, i.e.\ $e^{tX}$ is $\mu$-integrable and
$\E_\mu[e^{tX}] \le \exp(\sigma t^2/2)$ for every $t \in \bbr$. Then for every constant
$c \in \bbr$, the scaled variable $\omega \mapsto c\,X(\omega)$ is sub-Gaussian with
variance proxy $c^2\sigma$:
\[
\E_\mu\!\left[e^{t\,cX}\right] \le \exp\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\,c^2\sigma\,t^2\right)
\qquad\text{for all } t \in \bbr.
\]
